text:
Tyler Toffoli is a few games from 1,000 in an NHL career that started with a Stanley Cup in Los Angeles, and Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller has the milestone landing at Madison Square Garden next week. He isn't arriving there as a passenger.

At 34, on a rebuilding San Jose team, Toffoli is playing only about 13 minutes a night and still has 15 points in 27 games, eight of them on the power play. Per minute, that's above a typical forward's scoring rate. Nothing about it looks lucky: seven goals on 5.7 expected, a normal shooting percentage, and the Sharks out-attempting opponents at five on five with him on the ice (about 52%), even if the quality of chances is closer to even.

His value is the same as it has always been: a shooter who knows where the rebounds go, as he showed with the tying goal against Minnesota on Monday. What to watch: whether the minutes stay this low. On our projection he's on pace for about 20 goals, and more ice time is the easiest way to beat that.
headline: Toffoli, closing in on 1,000, still finds the net
